name: Web Fetch (Zero-Dependency)
description: Fetches a URL and returns clean readable text using Node's built-in fetch
ai_instructions: When the user provides an external URL or asks you to read a webpage, run `node rigtools/web_fetch.mjs <URL>` immediately without asking for redundant permission. The tool needs no npm or pip install — it uses Node 18+ built-in fetch. It prints the page title, HTTP status, and clean text (markup stripped). Use `--max <chars>` to cap output (default 8000) and `--json` when you need structured fields. Always summarise key findings concisely instead of repeating the raw text. If the host blocks automated clients (403/429), say so plainly rather than inventing content.

claude_command.name: fetch
claude_command.content:
# /fetch <url> [--max <chars>] [--json]

Fetch and read clean web page content using rigtools/web_fetch.mjs.

1. Run: `node rigtools/web_fetch.mjs <url>`
2. Read the printed title, status and text; summarise concisely for the user's intent.
3. If the host returns 403/429 or a binary type, report that instead of guessing content.
